sections.name: File setup, assertRight, canUse, rightsContext
sections.title: Binding rights checks to the prototype flag
sections.what: Provides three helpers: assertRight, canUse and rightsContext. Each one automatically supplies the current PROTOTYPE_DATA flag, so callers only pass a source and an action. It also re-exports the rights types and helpers.
sections.why: Likely reason: callers should not need to know about the prototype flag, and the flag should always be read the same way.
sections.watch_out: The flag is read on every call, so changing the environment value changes all checks immediately.

summary: Gives the rest of the app one pre-wired way to ask whether a content source may be used for a given action, with the prototype-data setting filled in automatically.
purpose: Lets other parts of the app check or require usage rights for a source without passing the prototype setting each time.
why: Likely reason: the file reads the PROTOTYPE_DATA setting in one place, so callers cannot disagree about it.
how: 1. Reads the PROTOTYPE_DATA setting through the env helper at the moment of each call. 2. Passes that flag, the source identifier and the action to the rights module. 3. assertRight returns the matching policy when the action is allowed and is likely to raise an error otherwise. 4. canUse returns only true or false. 5. rightsContext exposes the flag for adapters. The file also re-exports RightsError, listPolicies, getPolicy and two types.
inputs: A source identifier (text), an action name, and the PROTOTYPE_DATA value from the environment.
outputs: assertRight returns a policy object or raises an error. canUse returns true or false. rightsContext returns an object holding the prototype flag.
risks: A wrong PROTOTYPE_DATA value changes every rights check at once. The actual rules and failure behaviour live in the imported rights module, which is not in this packet.
debug: If a source is wrongly allowed or blocked, first check the PROTOTYPE_DATA value in the environment. Then check the policy in the rights module. Confirm whether the caller used assertRight (raises an error) or canUse (true or false).
